title: VPC Preflight: Terraform Compatibility + Quota & Resource Scanner
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a deterministic preflight scanner that validates Terraform module versions, cloud quotas, IAM surface, DNS delegation, and GPU SKU availability before Private (VPC) installs. The goal is a single CLI and CI-friendly check that outputs an actionable report and optionally offers guided auto-remediation steps (non-destructive by default). This ticket covers design, implementation of cloud probes (GCP/AWS/Azure), Terraform state inspection and module compatibility matrix checks, and integration with the VPC onboarding flow.
acceptance_criteria: CLI command 'rw-preflight scan <workspace>' returns non-zero exit on critical failures and provides machine-readable JSON report

Checks cover: terraform module versions & compatibility, project/billing quotas, IAM roles/policies existence & least-privilege flags, DNS delegation + required records, GPU SKU availability in target region
Report contains remediation steps and links to the documented runbook, and a 'dry-run auto-fix' list for selective fixes
Integration test harness with mocked cloud APIs and a live smoke run against staging Tenant-42
Documentation + console UI hook to show preflight report in the Private onboarding flow
implementation_steps: Design compatibility matrix schema for supported terraform module versions and runtime changes
Prototype cloud quota probes for AWS/GCP/Azure using vendor APIs (compute quotas, GPUs, regional quotas, service enablement)
Implement IAM surface validation: cross-check expected roles/service accounts and flag overly-broad policies
DNS checks: NS delegation, required A/CNAME/TXT for control plane, and validation of private DNS zones where applicable
GPU SKU probe: query SKU availability and estimated capacity by region, and add a heuristic for minimum available nodes based on requested capacity
Terraform state inspection: parse backend config and detect unsupported module versions or deprecated inputs

Wire CLI output to JSON and human summary; add optional '--apply-fixes' for: enabling APIs, creating service accounts (with minimal policy templates), and adding DNS records (only when explicit flags provided)
Add fast-fail hooks for public-cloud quotas that would block installs and softer warnings for cost/rate-limit risks
Add CI integration (GitHub Action) to run preflight on PRs touching private-deploy Terraform
links: https://confluence.company/redwood/private-preflight-design (design doc — compatibility schema and probe spec)
notes_and_tradeoffs: Trade-off: deeper cloud quotas require service-account level access to query detailed quota usage. For initial rollout we use read-only aggregated quota APIs and surface remaining limits, with an opt-in path for customers to provide elevated read-only roles for more precise checks

Decision: auto-remediation will be conservative: only enable non-destructive operations or create service accounts with explicit consent. Any IAM policy changes are suggested as code snippets by default
Risk: GPU SKU availability changes rapidly; we include a freshness timestamp and recommend fallback model variants in the onboarding flow instead of relying solely on reservation
Scope: This ticket focuses on probes and report generation. Full auto-provisioning (Terraform apply on customer account) is out-of-scope and will be tracked separately
test_plan: Unit tests for compatibility matrix validation and Terraform module parsing
Integration tests: mocked cloud APIs for AWS/GCP/Azure to validate probe paths
E2E staging run: run preflight against Tenant-42 with real limited-access creds and verify report and suggested fixes
Chaos test: simulate throttled quota APIs and ensure graceful degradation and retry/backoff behavior
